ORIGINAL USMLE-STYLE PRACTICE

Antibiotic principles and resistance: 2

A bacterial strain expresses more membrane pumps and maintains low intracellular concentrations of a protein-synthesis inhibitor. The ribosomal target is unchanged. Which resistance mechanism explains why adequate extracellular concentrations no longer produce the expected response?

  1. Modification of the drug target
  2. Reduced outer-membrane permeability
  3. Biofilm-associated persistence
  4. Increased drug efflux
  5. Enzymatic drug inactivation
Answer and explanation

Increased drug efflux

Transport pumps can lower intracellular antibiotic exposure.

Option explanations

Increased drug efflux: Transport pumps can lower intracellular antibiotic exposure.

Enzymatic drug inactivation: Bacteria can produce enzymes that destroy or chemically modify an antibiotic. This does not best answer the specific question in this case.

Modification of the drug target: A changed target can bind the antibiotic less effectively while maintaining its microbial function. This does not best answer the specific question in this case.

Reduced outer-membrane permeability: Loss or alteration of porins can reduce entry of antibiotics into Gram-negative bacteria. This does not best answer the specific question in this case.

Biofilm-associated persistence: Organisms in biofilms can be difficult to eradicate; device management may be needed despite planktonic susceptibility. This does not best answer the specific question in this case.
